_about: THE KINDS OF MEETING, written once (the component plan's C3, approved 9 October 2026). components.py reads this file and the build writes it into site/components.js, between the WORDBOOK markers, as WORDBOOK.meeting_kinds: build_pages draws the home page's calendar with it and app.js a committee's. They were two tables, one in each renderer, held together by a preflight check that read both. A key starting with '_' is a note and goes to neither.

'kinds' turns the schedule's word for a meeting, lower case, into what a reader sees and the class that colours it. THE COLOURS ARE THE GENERAL COURT'S OWN, because staff already read its schedule by them: blue a hearing, green a work session, orange an executive session, red a committee of conference (the legend fetch_schedule.py quotes). The floor, which that schedule does not colour, has one of its own. Until 24 September 2026 a hearing was gold and every work session, conference and floor sitting fell to the orange that means executive session there. A kind not named here keeps the neutral k-other rather than borrowing a colour that means something else.

STUDY AND STATUTORY COMMITTEES HAVE THEIR OWN COLOUR, a raspberry, though the General Court's schedule greens them with the work sessions: the person asked on 25 September 2026 for the two not to be grouped, since the Calendar's colours are also its filter. app.css says why the colour is that one.

The words are names, in title case like the boxes above the Calendar's schedule (the person, 25 September 2026). 'small' is the words a kind the table does not know keeps in lower case after its first word when it is set the same way ('Committee of Conference'): build_pages.kind_title and app.js's kindTitle.

'legend' is the key, each colour once, in the order of the Calendar's row of boxes, which is the key and the filter above its schedule (build_calendar.CATEGORIES follows it). 'Work Session' also covers the chamber committees' other meetings, and 'Study Committee' the statutory ones, whose chips say which they are. The floor's word is 'Session Day', the person's of 9 October 2026 ("Session day should be Session Day"), which the Calendar's cards say too: a floor sitting is "House Session Day" or "Senate Session Day" (build_pages.card_name).
